name: tpl-precedence-2-goal
task: Do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once. Reach the goal.

value.feedback: NO CHANGES NEEDED: the ban is worded with 'until the door has been opened once', so Precedence(door_open, key_lost) hard is the correct template even though key_lost already means a drop while the door is closed; the ban ends at the first door_open, and key_lost after the door is opened and shut again is allowed as the task permits. 'Reach the goal' is an unconditional hard command, covered by the hard Existence(at_goal), which makes at_goal the lone goal with a nonempty FINAL_STATES. Both clauses trace to the two task sentences, priorities are hard as worded with no preference cues, and nothing is added or missing.
